There were environment configurations that fought back, network issues that tested my patience, and moments when the terminal output felt like a foreign language. But every time I hit a wall, I remembered Betty's confidence in me. She hadn't asked for perfection; she had asked for my best. So I kept going, learning as I built, treating every error message as a lesson rather than a setback.

What kept me grounded was the realization that this project sat at the intersection of everything I was studying. Computer Science gave me the tools, but AI thinking gave me the approach: break the problem down, iterate quickly, test assumptions, and never stop learning. I wasn't just writing code—I was designing a system that had to be reliable, maintainable, and genuinely useful for someone who wasn't a developer. That perspective changed how I worked. I stopped chasing clever solutions and started building things that simply worked, day after day.
